diagnostics.message: :module.forge_trust_validator_lambda: explicit depends_on of :resource.aws_cloudwatch_log_group.forge_trust_validator_lambda is redundant — already implied by attribute references
:resource.aws_cloudwatch_event_target.forge_trust_validator_lambda: explicit depends_on of :module.forge_trust_validator_lambda is redundant — already implied by attribute references

module.forge_trust_validator_lambda has an explicit depends_on on aws_cloudwatch_log_group.forge_trust_validator_lambda, but it already depends on that log group implicitly via `logging_log_group = aws_cloudwatch_log_group.forge_trust_validator_lambda.name`. The depends_on is redundant.

aws_cloudwatch_event_target.forge_trust_validator_lambda has an explicit depends_on on module.forge_trust_validator_lambda, but it already depends on the module implicitly via `arn = module.forge_trust_validator_lambda.lambda_function_arn`. The depends_on is redundant.

null_resource.update_forge_role_trust updates each Forge role's assume-role policy to trust the trust-validator Lambda role (`arn:aws:iam::...:role/${var.prefix}-forge-trust-validator`), which is created by module.forge_trust_validator_lambda. It has no dependency on the module, so Terraform can grant trust before that role exists. It should depend on the module so the Lambda role is created first.
